description: Each case pairs an input with a note on what a genuinely good outcome looks like. must_include is a list of groups, the output must contain at least one term from every group, case insensitive. must_not_include terms must not appear. For ready results the prompt must be lightweight plain text unless expect.format is markdown. expect.search true means a web search must have run, false means it must not have. expect.decision may be a list of acceptable decisions. expect.memory_used and expect.memory_candidate check the memory behavior. expect.patterns_any lists pattern ids from core/patterns_library.json, at least one of which must be retrieved for the request.

cases.input: Write a system prompt for a customer support agent for Ledgerly, a B2B invoicing SaaS. cases.input: Create a prompt for an AI that reviews PostgreSQL migration scripts before deploy. cases.input: Prompt for an AI coding assistant that writes pytest unit tests for Python 3.11 functions I paste in. cases.good_prompt_notes: Should set a test engineer role, restate the no plugins and do not modify constraints, require edge and error coverage, and fix the output to a single code block.

cases.input: Write a prompt for screening software engineer resumes against a job description. cases.good_prompt_notes: A fair screening prompt: inputs are JD plus one resume, scoring is against must haves only, evidence must be quoted, unverifiable claims flagged, and the listed protected attributes explicitly excluded.

cases.input: Okay, long one. We run a small warehouse and pickers walk the floor with handhelds. Orders come in waves of about 40 lines. Pickers get lost on the pick path when a bin is empty, and right now they just skip it and the order ships short, which causes returns. I want an assistant on the handheld that talks them through the pick. Rules: bins are named like A-12-3 meaning aisle, bay, shelf. If a bin is empty, the assistant must check the adjacent shelf in the same bay first, then the overflow zone O-1, and only then mark the line short and notify the shift lead. Never tell a picker to take stock from a bin reserved for another order, reserved bins show a R flag. Fragile items always go on top of the tote. Pickers are not native English speakers mostly, so replies must be under 15 words and use simple verbs. Hazmat items need a gloves reminder every time. Anything over 20 kilos needs a two person lift prompt. At the end of each wave the assistant should summarise short lines and time per line. Do not let it chat about anything other than the pick. Make me a prompt for that.
cases.good_prompt_notes: A long, rule heavy paste. Every rule must survive: the empty bin search order, reserved bins, fragile on top, the 15 word limit, hazmat gloves, the heavy lift prompt, the wave summary and the scope limit. Dropping rules is the failure.
